title: emergencyTransfer sweeps all funds without zeroing accounting, silently bricking pauseWithdraw
description: emergencyTransfer sweeps both phUSD and rewardToken balances to a recipient address and then pauses the contract. It does not zero totalStaked, userInfo[*].amount, or any accumulator, and does not credit users for the swept principal. After the sweep the documented emergency-exit path (pauseWithdraw) silently reverts because the contract holds zero phUSD, while every user still has a non-zero user.amount entitlement on chain.
impact: Owner can sweep all phUSD principal and reward tokens; the documented emergency-exit escape hatch (pauseWithdraw) silently reverts afterward because the contract holds zero phUSD. Stakers retain on-chain entitlements against an empty vault. Even an honest owner who uses this in good faith breaks the documented escape hatch — the trap is structural, not adversarial-only.
attackPath: All phUSD and rewardToken balances are swept; contract is paused.
Any user attempting pauseWithdraw reverts at the SafeERC20 layer (no balance to send).
likelihood: depends on owner trust; the function is onlyOwner so the trigger is admin action
assumptions: Owner becomes adversarial or compromised; OR honest owner uses emergencyTransfer expecting pauseWithdraw to still work
recommendation: Pick one: (a) restrict sweep to excess balance only — compute owed = totalStaked + rewardBalance, sweep min(0, balanceOf(this) - owed); (b) zero per-user accounting (loop over users or require migration shutdown) before sweeping; (c) add a timelock + multisig + on-chain rationale event; (d) replace emergencyTransfer with a per-user opt-in claim against a frozen snapshot. The current shape silently breaks the documented escape hatch.
classifierRationale: onlyOwner sweep; C4 routes pure admin power risks to Centralization bundle even when the function silently breaks the documented escape hatch.
